mentions.name: DIY bright lamp
mentions.description: This project builds a DIY high-brightness lamp similar to commercial products like Brighter or Rhythm, but for a few hundred dollars instead of $1-2k. The parts are specced, the hardware is designed, and the firmware is built; a first LED test against a bench supply will produce hard numbers on whether a chunky aluminum heatsink with Noctua PC fans can cool the full 500+ W final version.
mentions.problem: Comparable commercial bright lamps like Brighter and Rhythm cost $1-2k.
mentions.source_excerpt: Project #2: Building a DIY bright-ass lamp, like Brighter [3] or Rhythm [4], but for a few hundred bucks instead of $1-2k. I've specced out the parts, designed the hardware, and built the firmware. Later today I'll do my first LED test against a bench supply, to get some hard numbers for if my cooling solution (a chunky aluminum heatsink and some Noctua PC fans) is sufficient for the full 500+ W final version.
